title: SEC seeks public comments on draft notification governing stablecoin transactions conducted through digital asset business operators
key_claim: Draft rules cap stablecoin transfers in or out of a licensed digital asset operator at 5 million baht per customer per day, prohibit transfers to or from another person's account or wallet, and close for comment on 26 November 2026.
frame_summary: The SEC presents the draft as anti-money-laundering supervision of stablecoin flows through licensed operators, binding each transfer to the customer's own verified accounts.
verbatim_quote: Transfers of stablecoins from or to an account or wallet belonging to another person are prohibited.
verbatim_list: limited separately to 5 million baht per customer per day with each DA operator
The public hearing period ends on 26 November 2026.
must be an account or wallet that has been verified as belonging to the same customer conducting such transfer

title: Regulations for the Operations of Non-Security Virtual Assets in Nigeria
date_evidence: Released on Thursday, 5 November 2026, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) (Technext, 06/11/2026, reporting the release of this PDF; the PDF itself carries no date line)
key_claim: In a platform P2P trade a provider may not release a regulated token unless the name and BVN of the paying or receiving naira account match the verified customer; value sent to an unhosted wallet counts as a cross-border transaction unless the wallet is verified as controlled by the customer or another Nigerian resident.
frame_summary: The CBN builds a licensing perimeter that ties every naira-to-token conversion to a verified identity and treats unverified self-custody transfers as cross-border flows.

title: Competing rails for crossborder payments: banks, fintechs, and stablecoins (BIS Working Paper 1385)
key_claim: Where stablecoins undercut bank and fintech costs on cross-border transfers, the advantage reflects distortions associated with capital controls rather than the technology, and liquidity between dollar stablecoins and non-US currencies is very thin.
frame_summary: Argues that stablecoins are not a cheaper payment technology in general; their edge in some corridors is an arbitrage of capital controls.
verbatim_quote: this advantage reflects distortions associated with capital controls rather than the underlying technology
verbatim_list: liquidity between US dollar stablecoins and non-US currencies is generally very thin
demonstrate that stablecoins are not a panacea for frictions in cross-border payments

title: Dollarisation and monetary control: what lessons for the rise of stablecoins? (BIS Working Paper 1370)
key_claim: Across more than 130 economies, stablecoin flows appear largely unaffected by broad or specific capital flow restrictions, unlike deposit dollarisation, likely because stablecoins partly circulate outside the regulatory perimeter.
frame_summary: Argues that capital flow restrictions which once contained deposit dollarisation do not bite on stablecoins, because the flows run outside the regulated perimeter.
verbatim_quote: stablecoin flows seem to be largely unaffected by either broad or specific capital flow restrictions
verbatim_list: This likely occurs because stablecoins are partly circulating outside the regulatory perimeter.
notes: Structural anchor (3-6 month band): the canonical evidence that conventional capital flow measures miss stablecoin flows. Read by WebFetch on 16/11/2026. Independent WebFetch check on 16/11/2026: quote and all list spans FOUND-EXACT.

title: Ativos virtuais no câmbio: a Resolução BCB 561 entrou em vigor e estes prazos já correm
key_claim: Since 1 October 2026 Brazil's Resolution BCB 561 bars virtual assets, including stablecoins, from settling payments between an eFX provider and its counterparty abroad, with a US$10,000 per-operation limit on certain eFX transfers.
frame_summary: A Brazilian law firm explains that Resolution 561 does not ban virtual assets but closes stablecoins as a settlement route in the regulated foreign-exchange channel.

title: CBN Sets N15bn Capital Requirement For Foreign Stablecoin Issuers, Tightens Dollar Token Rules
key_claim: Class 2 foreign-currency stablecoin issuers need at least N15 billion of capital and a Nigerian-incorporated entity, and the naira leg of a Class 2 P2P trade must be settled through, or reported to, a CBN-designated authorised dealer.
frame_summary: Reports the CBN rules as a tightening of dollar-token activity that routes foreign-currency stablecoins through local entities and the authorised-dealer FX system.

title: IMF wants Kenya to ease stablecoin reserve rules, review crypto capital thresholds

frame_summary: Reports the IMF pushing Kenya to loosen a localisation rule, a counter-current to onshoring stablecoin reserves.
